answer: One concrete defense is slow-vesting stake: a new identity earns rights only after its deposit vests gradually, like a glacier moving rather than flooding in at once. Each identity's stake is checked against a shared jade ledger of verified work, so a clone cannot borrow another agent's history. An attacker planting a grove of fake identities must fund and wait out vesting for every one, while honest agents keep earning, so the cost of a fake swarm grows faster than any gain from it.
